scope: Offline static audit of stock sagit TZ and stock XBL ClockDxe; no device access, no runtime measurement and no secure-boot attestation.

analysis_copy.normalization: Only clear malformed PE debug-directory RVA/size in the analysis copy. Original debug directory size is 225, not a multiple of IMAGE_DEBUG_DIRECTORY size. Code and data bytes from RVA/file offset 0x1000 onward are byte-identical to stock. Original firmware remains unchanged.

stock_clockdxe.cpu_source_registration: 0x8ab0 registers source IDs 105 and 106 using base 0x17800000 plus descriptors at 0x17350/0x17370.
initial_sequence: Clock_InitImage calls PLL Config enums 10 and 12 for sources 105/106; Agera HAL 0xddec sets USER_CTL(+0x0c) output bits 3 and 0.
Cluster0 is enabled, switched to auxiliary mux record 0x15570, then switched to the version-selected local PLL record from 0x7a20.
The chip version query is DalChipInfo method offset 0x48 (or remote method offset 0x58). 0x7ac0 compares version with 0x20000; 0x7ac4 selects the v2 record at 0x15538 for version >=2.0.
The v1 local PLL record at 0x15458 uses L=77. The v2 record at 0x154a8 uses L=81. With 19.2MHz reference these correspond to 1478.4MHz and 1555.2MHz; these are configured rates, not measurements.
Cluster1 is enabled and switched to auxiliary record 0x155a8; it need not be using its local PLL at handoff.

cpu_mux_update.behavior: Preserves unrelated CFG bits, maps source ID to selector, encodes HID as nDiv2x-1, writes CMD UPDATE and loops until UPDATE clears. Local PLL record implies CFG fields 0x301; auxiliary record implies fields 0x403. No claim that these exact values remain live after later firmware clients run.

cpu_pll_lock.warning: CPU sources 105/106 select the Agera status-register lock path. GCC GPLL0 Fabia MODE bit31 is not the CPU PLL lock predicate. A disabled local PLL is valid while the cluster uses an auxiliary clock.

stock_clockdxe.exit_boot_services: The stock image does not contain standard ExitBootServices or ReadyToBoot event-group GUID byte strings. This absence alone does not prove the absence of a legacy event callback or later secure-firmware ownership. EFI exit is not a hardware PLL/OSM ownership acknowledgment.

tz_initialization_failure.post_table_failure: After descriptor-driven writes, 0x1c094058 calls 0x1c094d14. That function can return -1 if lookup, frequency setup or enable of gcc_glm_clk / apcs_common_lmh_clk fails. The parent returns -1 without setting its private once flag.
tz_initialization_failure.success_tail: Only the successful post-table path programs fuse-derived OSM offsets 0x404/0x410 and writes 0x179d4020 to 0x179c1050 and 0x179c3050. The initializer then sets private byte 0x1c109e20 to 1.
outer_fatal_checks: 0x1c01b770 checks sub_1c0664c8 and has a fatal loop
0x1c01bb64 checks sub_1c0664c8 and has a fatal path
tz_initialization_failure.conclusion: The outer fatal branches do not propagate the OSM initializer error because the intervening wrapper discards it and returns zero. Reaching HLOS therefore is not proof that the full OSM/TZ initialization succeeded. This conclusion is specific to the observed return chain; it is not a claim that every failure in the firmware is recoverable.
tz_initialization_failure.success_tail_not_written_earlier: Independent descriptor review found no earlier write to either +0x1050: v2 block destinations are +0x500 (192 words), +0x170 (49 words), +0x300 (95 words); matching single-register descriptors are +0x4,+0x12c,+0x134,+0x260,+0x268,+0x120,+0x128,+0x130. The vendor Linux clock-osm source has no +0x1050 read precedent; nonsecure access must not be inferred merely from a mapped aperture.

handoff_boundary: The bridge may establish compatible retained register state and an HLOS lifecycle policy. A small set of permitted SEQ parameter reads is not a checksum of all sequencer code/branches, proof of completed PLL setup, or proof that no secure master can alter hardware.

The audited legacy XBL ClockDxe actively changes CPU mux and PLL configuration after the secure boot stage. CPU PLL ownership cannot be assigned wholly to TZ from the no-TZ Linux fallback implementation.

Do not require both cluster PLLs to be enabled at admission; cluster1 can validly use the auxiliary clock. Do not add speculative CPU MMIO admission gates without a supported nonsecure access contract.

A tail-state read such as both OSM+0x1050 pointers can distinguish some post-table failures if proven HLOS-readable and absent from earlier matching descriptor writes. It remains compatibility evidence, not a completion attestation.
The original boot chain remains a prerequisite. No post-ExitBootServices EFI Clock protocol calls, no 0x10009 suffix calls, and no direct CPU PLL retuning are justified by this audit.
